verifications.claim: Only three golfers in history have won back-to-back Masters tournaments, successfully defending their title at Augusta National: Jack Nicklaus (1965–1966), Nick Faldo (1989–1990), and Tiger Woods (2001–2002).
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'Jack Nicklaus: 1965-66; Nick Faldo: 1989-90; Tiger Woods: 2001-02' ... 'Over two decades later, no champion has managed to successfully defend since.'; R3/R4/R5: include 'Rory McIlroy: 2025-26' as fourth back-to-back winner.
verifications.reasoning: R1/R2 support exactly three; R3/R4/R5 list four including McIlroy, creating direct contradiction.

verifications.claim: No golfer has won three consecutive Masters tournaments.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'To date, no one has ever won three Masters titles in a row.'; R2: 'Has anyone won the masters three times in a row? To date, no one has ever won three Masters titles in a row.'; R3: 'Has any golfer won three Masters in a row? No...'; R5: 'No one has ever won three straight tournaments.'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly confirm no three consecutive wins.

verifications.claim: Jack Nicklaus was the first to win back-to-back Masters tournaments.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'it wasn't until 1965-66... His name was Jack Nicklaus... became the first back-to-back champion'; R2: 'Jack Nicklaus became the first back-to-back champion'; R3: 'Nicklaus was the first golfer to ever win consecutive Masters tournaments.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Nicklaus was the first.

verifications.claim: Jack Nicklaus won the 1965 Masters by nine strokes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'In 1965, Nicklaus beat Palmer by nine strokes'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on margin and year.

verifications.claim: Jack Nicklaus won the 1966 Masters in an 18-hole playoff.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'the following year [1966], he won an 18-hole playoff against Tommy Jacobs and Gay Brewer.'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on playoff format and year.

verifications.claim: Nick Faldo won the 1989 Masters in a playoff defeating Scott Hoch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'in 1989... Scott Hoch missed a two-foot par putt... Faldo... holing a 25-footer for birdie'; R3: 'Faldo and Scott Hoch... playoff... Faldo drained a long birdie putt'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of playoff win over Hoch in 1989.

verifications.claim: Nick Faldo won the 1990 Masters in a playoff defeating Raymond Floyd.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'The following year [1990], Faldo... defeating Raymond Floyd in a playoff.'; R3: 'His second consecutive... also went to a playoff... Raymond Floyd'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of playoff win over Floyd in 1990.

verifications.claim: Tiger Woods is the most recent player to win back-to-back Masters tournaments.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'Over two decades later, no champion has managed to successfully defend since [Woods 2001-02].'; R3/R4/R5: McIlroy '2025-26' is latest/most recent repeat winner.
verifications.reasoning: R1/R2 support Woods as most recent; R3/R4/R5 state McIlroy (2025-26) as most recent, contradicting.

verifications.claim: Tiger Woods secured his second and third green jackets in 2001–2002.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: Woods won '1997'... then '2001'... 'The following year [2002]'; R3: 'Woods’ second and third green jackets came in 2001 and 2002.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Woods' first jacket 1997, second/third in 2001-2002.
